label: At GO early in the episode: high after reaching S2, low after S1, higher if unrewarded.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * np.maximum(60 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(60 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S2 r') * np.maximum(60 - ep_trial, 0)
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * np.maximum(50 - ep_trial, 0)
explanation: Fires only at GO, and its scale decays over the first ~50 trials of the episode (timing). Beyond timing, the magnitude is set by the previous trial: raised when the last reached state was S2, lowered when it was S1, with an extra boost when the last trial was unrewarded, all scaled by an early-episode ramp max(50 - ep_trial, 0). This is an interaction with timing, not an additive offset. The free fit adds a rare a1->S2 boost (a1 S2 u/r is under-predicted by the short form), an extra S2-unrewarded boost and small trial-before terms; belief_lo adds almost nothing. No future variables used. Silent at D1 and D2.

terms: (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S2 r') * np.maximum(60 - ep_trial, 0)
(phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S2 r') * np.maximum(60 - ep_trial, 0)

issues: The label says 'higher if unrewarded' as if it applies everywhere, but the profile residuals show reward has no effect after S1 (GO after a1 S1 r -0.220 vs a1 S1 u -0.229; a2 S1 r -0.215 vs a2 S1 u -0.224). The reward effect only appears after S2, and there it is mostly the common-rewarded case a2 S2 r (+0.088) sitting low against the other S2 histories (+0.27 to +0.45).

The recorded prev_reward==0 term adds only a little: on test, the 2-term S2/S1 ramp scores 0.616 and the recorded 3-term form scores 0.651. Its weight (+0.008) is small next to the state terms (+0.017 / -0.022).

Misses on the recorded short form show clear systematic errors by previous trial at GO. Under-predicted: a1 S2 u +0.186, a1 S2 r +0.094, a2 S2 u +0.071. Over-predicted: a2 S2 r -0.088, a2 S1 u -0.066, a1 S1 u -0.065. Because the reward term is shared across both states, it pushes the S1-unrewarded cases too high and can't separate a2 S2 r from the other S2 histories.

Swapping the reward term for last_is('a2 S2 r') * ramp raises test R^2 beyond timing to 0.690 (ramp 50) and 0.692 (ramp 60). The leftover systematic errors shrink: largest is GO after a1 S2 u +0.127, every other cell is within 0.06.

The other targeted variants don't beat it on test: prev_common==0 0.634, stay==0 0.622, last_is('a1 S2 u') 0.654, 'reward mismatches state' 0.630. Ramp lengths 30/40/70/80 also score lower (0.559/0.649/0.671/0.639).

The checks that held up: the feature is silent at D1 and D2, the core effect is S2 vs S1 on the previous trial scaled by an early-episode ramp, belief adds nothing, and no future or model-output variables are used.
